turns.t: Hello, doctor. The surgery rang to say my calcium was high on a routine blood test, and I'm not sure what that means.
I'm her daughter, I came along because Mum gets confused with medical talk. ~
Thank you both for coming. A high calcium result is something we should look into. Have you noticed any symptoms?
I've been tired lately, I suppose. And thirsty.
She's been constipated too, she told me last week.
How long has the tiredness been going on?
Oh, a couple of months, I'd say. I put it down to the weather.
Any tummy pain, nausea, or bone pain?
No pain in the bones. No nausea.
Any kidney stones in the past?
No. Never.
What medicines are you taking?
Just a calcium and vitamin D tablet, one a day, for my bones.
No, Mum, it's two a day. I fill the dosette box.
Is it? I only take the one in the morning.
You take one in the morning and one at night, I see you do it.
I'll note that the two of you remember it differently, and we'll check the pharmacy record.
I can ring the pharmacy while you're talking, doctor. ~
Please do. Do you have any allergies to medicines?
No, none.
Any other conditions?
Osteoporosis. That's why I take the tablets.
Do you smoke or drink?
No smoking. A sherry at Christmas.
Doctor, I've checked her observations. Pulse 68, blood pressure 138 over 80.
Thank you. These are fine. I'd like to feel your neck and tummy, if you don't mind. ~
Go on.
No lumps in the neck, and your abdomen is soft.
What causes a high calcium? ~
Several things, including too much calcium from tablets, or an overactive gland in the neck. Right now I can't say which it is. ~
The pharmacy confirms two tablets a day, doctor. ~
Thank you. Then that is the first thing to adjust. ~
Should I stop them? ~
Please hold them until I have the repeat blood test, and I'll phone you with the result.
All right. Thank you. ~

chief_complaint.normalized_value: Incidental high calcium on blood test

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient says one calcium and vitamin D tablet a day; her daughter says two a day; pharmacy later confirmed two a day.

clinical_actions.description: Hold the calcium and vitamin D tablets until the repeat blood test

contradictions_detected: Calcium and vitamin D tablets: patient one a day vs daughter two a day (pharmacy later confirmed two).
